title: Chapter 2 Test: Storefront Development
description: Eighteen questions on responsive theme CSS, framework-free JavaScript, product pages, the cart and Ajax APIs, and the merchandising surfaces. Aim for 75%.

questions.prompt: A product card looks right in a 4-column grid but cramped inside a cart drawer at the same viewport width. What is the correct fix?
options: A viewport media query targeting narrow screens
A container query on the card's own inline size
A second card snippet with drawer-specific styles
A fixed pixel width on the drawer
questions.explanation: The viewport is identical in both contexts; only the available container width differs. `container-type: inline-size` plus `@container` lets one component respond to the space it is actually given, which is what makes a card reusable across grid, drawer, related products and search.

questions.prompt: Which of these are direct causes of Cumulative Layout Shift in a Shopify theme? Select all that apply.
options: Images rendered without width and height attributes
Content injected by apps after first paint
Using `clamp()` for font sizes
Web fonts swapping in with different metrics
questions.explanation: Missing intrinsic dimensions, late-injected content and font metric swaps are the three big CLS sources in themes. `clamp()` is resolved at layout time and does not itself cause shift — the fix for images is `image_tag`, which emits width and height from the real aspect ratio.

questions.prompt: Why does `minmax(0, 1fr)` fix grid overflow where `1fr` does not?
options: `1fr` is invalid in `repeat()`
`1fr` has an automatic minimum size, so a long title or wide image can force the column wider
`minmax` enables container queries
`1fr` does not respect gap
questions.explanation: `1fr` is shorthand for `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, and the `auto` minimum means the track cannot shrink below its content. Setting the minimum to 0 lets the track shrink and the content wrap or scroll — this one substitution fixes most 'grid overflows on mobile' bugs.

questions.prompt: Which custom element lifecycle behaviour makes web components particularly well suited to Shopify themes?
options: Shadow DOM isolates theme CSS from app CSS
`connectedCallback` runs automatically when the theme editor re-renders a section or the cart drawer swaps in new HTML
Custom elements are server-rendered by Liquid
They can be defined without a hyphen in the tag name
questions.explanation: Sections are re-rendered and replaced constantly — by the theme editor, by cart mutations, by filtering. Custom elements re-initialise themselves on insertion and clean up on removal, which removes an entire category of re-binding bugs. Tag names must contain a hyphen.

questions.prompt: Interpolating Liquid directly into a JavaScript string literal, such as `var title = '{{ product.title }}'`, is acceptable as long as the value comes from Shopify rather than a customer.
questions.explanation: It breaks on any apostrophe and is an injection vector for any data a third party can write into the store. Use `<script type="application/json">{{ product | json }}</script>` and `JSON.parse` — correctly escaped and never executed.

questions.prompt: A customer clicks quickly through four sizes on a PDP that fetches re-rendered section HTML per change, and occasionally sees a price that does not match the selection. What is the defect?
options: The Section Rendering API caches per product
Concurrent requests resolve out of order; the fix is aborting the previous request
`replaceState` should be `pushState`
`selected_or_first_available_variant` ignores the variant parameter
questions.explanation: Without an AbortController or a discard-late-responses guard, a slower earlier request can land after a faster later one and render stale markup. Developers rarely reproduce it because they click slowly on fast connections.

questions.prompt: A cart contains the same variant twice with different line item properties. The customer changes the quantity on one of them. Which endpoint is correct?
options: update.js keyed by variant ID
change.js keyed by the line item key
add.js with a negative quantity
clear.js then re-add everything
questions.explanation: update.js is keyed by variant ID and cannot distinguish two lines sharing a variant. change.js targets a specific line by its key — the variant ID plus a hash of its properties — which is the only correct choice for per-line controls.

questions.prompt: Which are genuine advantages of updating the cart drawer via the Section Rendering API rather than rebuilding markup in JavaScript? Select all that apply.
options: Discount and price logic exists once, in Liquid
Merchant theme-editor settings apply automatically with no code change
Function-based and B2B catalog pricing are computed correctly server-side
It eliminates the network round trip
questions.explanation: Server rendering keeps one implementation of pricing and merchandising logic and gets Function discounts and B2B catalog prices right for free. It does not remove the round trip — that is its cost, and it is usually worth paying.

questions.prompt: An add-to-cart returns HTTP 422 with a `description` reading "You can only add 3 … to the cart." What should the UI do?
options: Show a generic error message to avoid exposing internals
Show Shopify's description and reset the quantity input to the maximum available
Retry the request three times
Silently reduce the quantity and add it anyway
questions.explanation: The description is customer-readable and contains the only useful information in the response — the actual available quantity. A customer told 'only 3 available' buys 3; a customer told 'something went wrong' leaves.

questions.prompt: Match each cart data mechanism to its correct use.

pairs.right: Data attached to a single line — engraving text, personalisation
Structured key/value on the whole cart — delivery date, PO number
Unstructured free-text customer instruction for the whole order
Internal metadata hidden from the customer but visible in the admin and APIs

questions.explanation: Merchandising teams request all four without distinguishing them. Properties are per-line and make identical lines distinct; attributes are structured and flow to Flow, Functions and integrations; the note is free text; the underscore prefix hides a key from customer-facing surfaces.

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript object should every Ajax cart URL be built from, so the storefront works under localised Markets paths like /en-gb/?
questions.explanation: `window.Shopify.routes.root` is populated via content_for_header and resolves to '/' or the localised prefix. Hard-coded '/cart/add.js' works in development and breaks for international customers. The Liquid equivalent is `{{ routes.cart_add_url }}`.

questions.prompt: Why should filter links use `value.url_to_add` and `value.url_to_remove` rather than constructing URLs in your own code?
options: Hand-built URLs are blocked by Shopify's CDN
Filter parameter names and escaping rules are non-obvious — metafield filters especially — and platform-provided URLs are always correct
Only platform URLs trigger the Section Rendering API
Constructed URLs break the canonical tag
questions.explanation: Filter parameters take forms like `filter.p.m.custom.safety_rating` with their own escaping rules. Hand-built URLs work for simple cases in development and break on a metafield filter whose value contains a space.

questions.prompt: A merchandising team asks for infinite scroll on collections. What is the strongest technical objection?
options: It cannot be built with the Section Rendering API
It makes the footer unreachable, breaks back-button behaviour unless carefully handled, and reduces crawlability
Shopify rate-limits the requests
It always fails Core Web Vitals
questions.explanation: Infinite scroll is buildable and can perform well, but the footer holds navigation and trust signals, history and scroll restoration need deliberate handling, and crawlers may not reach later pages. A load-more button layered over real pagination links avoids all three.

questions.prompt: Order these steps of an INP-friendly click handler, fastest perceived response first.
items: Set the loading state so the browser can paint
Yield to the browser for a frame
answer: Set the loading state so the browser can paint
Yield to the browser for a frame
questions.explanation: INP is measured from interaction to the next paint. Painting a loading state first, then yielding, means the metric records a few milliseconds rather than the whole request duration — and the customer gets immediate feedback either way.

questions.prompt: Why should a PDP render its initial price from `selected_or_first_available_variant` rather than the first variant with JavaScript correcting it?
options: The first variant object is not exposed in Liquid
It avoids a visible price flash and prevents a wrong price appearing in HTML that crawlers and ad platforms read
JavaScript cannot access variant prices
It is required by the Section Rendering API
questions.explanation: `selected_or_first_available_variant` resolves the `?variant=` parameter server-side, so deep links from email, ads and Google Shopping render the correct price in the HTML — good for the customer, structured data and LCP alike.

questions.prompt: Placing external video and 3D model markup inside a `<template>` element prevents any network request until it is cloned into the DOM.
questions.explanation: Template content is parsed but inert — no iframe, no scripts, no media fetches. Cloning on click is what turns a multi-megabyte PDP with several video embeds into one that loads media only on demand. Dawn's DeferredMedia implements exactly this.

questions.prompt: Complete the Liquid that splits a large collection across pages.
questions.explanation: Without a paginate tag the loop stops at the platform's default limit regardless of collection size, and merchandisers report that products are missing. The tag also exposes a `paginate` object with the page links you need for SEO-safe load-more.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest argument for building a small set of flexible storytelling sections rather than one bespoke section per campaign design?
options: Flexible sections render faster
Every bespoke section is permanent maintenance and QA surface that only you can change, while flexible sections let the brand team compose without a deployment
Shopify limits themes to twenty sections
Bespoke sections cannot use colour schemes
questions.explanation: Per-design sections accumulate into forty near-identical files nobody can audit, and every campaign becomes a developer ticket. Flexible sections with genuinely structural options move that work to the people who own the campaign — with a deliberate bespoke exception for the two or three moments a year that justify one.
